answer: The cheapest real defence: mix in randomly chosen human-authored live tasks that cannot be precomputed, because atlas only stays cheap while clones that dodge the live lane lose the epoch payout entirely. Concretely, bridge is enforced in the ledger: The ledger rejects byte-identical submissions, forcing each clone to generate distinct work. Any reef approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
